name: DRAFT

paper.title: From Exploration to Mastery: Enabling LLMs to Master Tools via Self-Driven Interactions

construction.unit: tool documentation of one API (its description text)
construction.kept_as: LLM-rewritten description, revised from real calls to the tool
construction.processing: per API, up to 5 rounds: Explorer writes a query + parameters and calls the tool; Analyzer suggests edits; Rewriter rewrites the doc and proposes the next exploration direction

organization.structure: one document per API (plus one summary per tool in the code), keyed by tool and API name
organization.stores: documentation set; per-API history of explored queries and doc versions used during refinement
organization.index: none (docs are looked up by tool/API id); text-embedding-ada-002 only for the query-diversity and stop checks

management.operations: rewrite the doc in place each round; stop when two consecutive versions barely differ (avg of cosine and BLEU > 0.75)
management.conflicts: Analyzer checks the doc against the actual tool output and flags inconsistencies

retrieval.query: the user task (split into subtasks in the released inference script)
retrieval.candidates: the benchmark's candidate tools for the query; their docs are in the prompt
retrieval.selection: the agent LLM picks a tool, then APIs, then parameters from the docs

use.context: revised tool and API documentation in place of the original docs
use.reasoning: tool-use agent (ReAct/DFSDT-style); the paper does not name the agent loop used for DRAFT rows

classify.note: The memory is the documentation itself. At use time the agent reads the docs of every candidate tool the benchmark gives for the query and picks among them; there is no similarity search over docs (Table 3 tests BM25/Contriever only as an extra analysis).

stages.ingestion: For each API, an Explorer LLM invents a natural user query and parameters from the current doc and actually calls the tool; a new query whose ada-002 embedding is too close (cosine >= 0.9) to an earlier one is rejected and regenerated.
stages.construction: An Analyzer LLM compares the doc with the observed call and result and writes edit suggestions; a Rewriter LLM rewrites the doc from the example, the suggestions and the revision history, and proposes where to explore next.
stages.organization: One revised description per API kept in the tool's documentation file; the code also writes a new tool-level summary after all its APIs are revised.
stages.update: The loop repeats up to 5 rounds per API and stops early when the average of embedding cosine and BLEU between consecutive versions exceeds 0.75.
stages.retrieval: No memory search: the agent receives the documentation of the candidate tools; in the released script an LLM picks a tool from tool summaries, then APIs from the tool doc, then parameters from the API doc.
stages.answer: The tool-use agent calls APIs and answers from their responses; the docs only change how it understands the tools.

summary: Rewrites human-written tool documentation into LLM-oriented documentation through an explore, analyze, rewrite loop driven by real tool calls, with a query-diversity check and a similarity-based stopping rule.
notes:
Venue: PDF header 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025'; arXiv comment and repo README say ICLR 2025 Oral (OpenReview QKBu1BOAwd, page not reachable from here). Memory here is procedural: the stored item is the tool's documentation, refined offline before any test task; it is not per-user or per-episode memory.
DESIGN: §2.1-2.4, Algorithm 1, §3.1 (φ=0.9, τ=0.75, max 5 rounds, GPT-4o backbone), App. C (prompts). Code: DRAFT.py at commit 324685d. Retrieval/use fields describe the released Inference_DFSDT.py because the paper does not describe how the agent reads the docs.

sources.code_note: Official repo linked in §3.1. Pinned at the latest commit 324685d (2025-08-09); DRAFT.py and the prompts were last changed 2025-03-25, after paper v2 (2025-02-26). DRAFT.py only covers ToolBench (RapidAPI calls); RestBench docs are released as finished files without their generation script. The released revised docs (dataset/*/tool_instruction/*_DRAFT.json) are the actual memory used for the scores.

headline: The memory is tool documentation: each API's description is rewritten by GPT-4o after it has actually called the tool, then frozen before testing.
Refinement stops per API when two consecutive versions are nearly the same (avg of cosine and BLEU > 0.75), at most 5 rounds.
The revised docs are longer: ToolBench API descriptions grow from 14 to 31 words on average, RestBench ones 3.6x (TMDB) to 6.9x (Spotify).

units.name: API documentation
units.role: the description the agent reads to decide whether and how to call an API
units.made_by: Rewriter LLM (GPT-4o), from explored calls and Analyzer suggestions

fields.name: description
fields.what: rewritten API description: purpose, parameters, response fields, error behaviour

fields.name: parameters
fields.what: required and optional parameter lists from the original doc, copied unchanged

fields.name: example
fields.what: one user query with its parameters, present for every API in the released DRAFT files but not written by DRAFT.py
fields.src: released dataset/ToolBench/tool_instruction/DRAFT.json; read by the parameter prompt in Inference_DFSDT.py L330-L340 (L336)

units.name: Tool summary
units.role: short description of a whole tool and its functions, used to choose a tool
units.made_by: LLM, after all APIs of the tool are revised (code only)

fields.name: tool_description
fields.what: '<tool> is a tool that can ...' with a numbered list of its functions

units.name: Refinement log (per API, during construction only)
units.role: working memory of the loop, shown to the three LLM roles

fields.name: explored queries
fields.what: all earlier queries and their embeddings; the Explorer sees the queries, not their results

fields.name: doc history
fields.what: every earlier version of the description, passed to Analyzer and Rewriter

fields.name: exploration direction
fields.what: Rewriter's advice on what to try next, passed to the next Explorer call

write.how: Explorer LLM writes a natural user query and the parameters to call the API, avoiding earlier queries and following the last suggested direction
reject the query if its ada-002 cosine to any earlier query is >= 0.9 and ask again with a 'too similar' note
run the real API with the parameters; the response is filtered by the API's response schema and cut to 2,048 characters
Analyzer LLM reads the current doc, this round's example and result, and the doc history, and writes suggestions (consistency with outputs, completeness, conciseness)
write.src: paper §2.3, Eq. 3, App. C; code DRAFT.py L342-L352

write.how: Rewriter LLM writes the new description and a direction for the next exploration
Δ = (cosine of ada-002 embeddings + BLEU) / 2 between the last two versions; stop if Δ > 0.75, else next round
write.out: the last version replaces the original description
write.src: paper Eq. 5, §3.1; code DRAFT.py L244-L255, L374-L381

write.how: an LLM writes one tool-level description from the revised API docs
write.note: code only, not in the paper

read.how: LLM splits the query into subtasks and orders them by dependency; it sees the candidate APIs with their DRAFT descriptions

read.scores: tool summaries of the query's candidate tools

read.how: LLM lists the APIs to call

read.scores: the API documentation, including its example
read.how: LLM writes the call parameters, then the API is called
LLM judges whether the subtask answer is adequate; if not, used APIs are excluded and the loop tries again

answer_context.sees: API responses for each subtask, then the subtask answers
answer_context.format: subtask answers are summarized into one final answer; the docs shape the tool, API and parameter choices, not the final prompt
excludes: explored examples other than the one stored per API

compression.what: revised vs original API description, ToolBench
compression.basis: Not a compression: the doc grows from 14.2 to 31.4 words on average over 1,006 APIs (our count on the released Initial.json and DRAFT.json). The paper reports no length figures.

compression.what: revised vs original API description, RestBench
compression.basis: Not a compression: TMDB 30.0 to 107.3 words (54 APIs), Spotify 14.6 to 99.9 words (40 APIs), our count on the released files.

paper_vs_code.paper: Explorer self-reflects and regenerates until the query is below the similarity threshold
paper_vs_code.code: at most 3 generations; the last query is kept even if still too similar

paper_vs_code.paper: Explorer conditions on earlier examples and their tool results (Eq. 1)
paper_vs_code.code: Explorer receives the earlier queries only, not their results
after all APIs of a tool are revised, an LLM rewrites the tool-level description, which is what the agent reads to pick a tool
every API in the released DRAFT docs carries a 'User Query' + 'Parameters' example that DRAFT.py does not produce; the parameter prompt tells the agent to use it

paper_vs_code.paper: Table 1 compares DRAFT with ReAct, DFSDT and EasyTool without naming the agent loop DRAFT runs in
paper_vs_code.code: the released inference script (named DFSDT) splits the query into subtasks and picks tool, APIs and parameters with an answer check and up to 5 retries

open_questions: Released DRAFT docs add a worked example per API that the original docs lack; no ablation separates the effect of the example from the rewritten description.
Table 1 does not say which agent loop the DRAFT rows use; if it is the released decompose-and-retry script, part of the gain over ReAct and DFSDT may come from the loop rather than the documentation.
The docs are refined with GPT-4o calling the same APIs that the test queries use, and no held-out-tool split is reported.

text: For each API, an Explorer writes a new test query and calls the real tool, an Analyzer compares the doc with what happened, and a Rewriter writes a new doc and a direction for the next try.
The loop stops when two versions barely differ or after 5 rounds; the last version replaces the original doc.

text: Nothing is searched: the agent reads the revised docs of the candidate tools the benchmark gives. In the released script an LLM picks a tool from tool summaries, APIs from the tool doc, and parameters from the API doc.
If an LLM check finds a subtask unanswered, it tries other APIs or tools, up to 5 times.

discussion.takeaway: Tool documentation can be treated as a memory the model writes for itself: letting GPT-4o call each API, critique the doc and rewrite it gives better tool use than the original or a one-shot rewrite (EasyTool), and the rewritten docs help other models too.

claims.claim: DRAFT docs beat ReAct, DFSDT and EasyTool on all three datasets and three agent models.
claims.evidence: GPT-4o CP%: TMDB 88 vs 79 (EasyTool), Spotify 70.17 vs 64.91 (DFSDT), ToolBench 51 vs 45. Table 1, §3.2

claims.claim: Docs refined by one model help other models (cross-model generalization).
claims.evidence: GPT-4o-refined docs lift GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3-70B; Llama-3-70B-refined docs also help on TMDB. Table 1, Fig. 7, §3.3

claims.claim: More rounds help up to a point, then docs get redundant and scores drop.
claims.evidence: Fig. 6 curves over rounds 1-5; App. E trajectory rounds 4-5

claims.claim: Both the diversity check and the adaptive stop matter.
claims.evidence: GPT-4o TMDB CP 88 → 84 without diversity, → 80 without adaptive stop. Table 2, Table 5

claims.claim: Revised docs also improve tool retrieval and read better to humans.
claims.evidence: BM25 NDCG@1 on TMDB 24.0 → 29.0 (Table 3); human raters prefer DRAFT docs for completeness 68% vs 4% on ToolBench (Table 4)

discussion.limits_src: The paper has no limitations section.
reading: The memory is built offline, once per API, before testing; there is no update from test episodes, so this is documentation refinement rather than memory that grows with use.
The released DRAFT docs contain a per-API usage example absent from the original docs and not produced by DRAFT.py; its contribution is not measured.
Win% is a ChatGPT pairwise judgement against ReAct, so ReAct is 50 by construction; CP% only checks that the gold API path appears as a subsequence of the calls made.
Test sets are small: the released files hold 100 ToolBench G3 queries, 100 TMDB and 57 Spotify queries, so one query moves CP by 1 to 1.75 points.
Refinement uses GPT-4o, and GPT-4o also scores best as the agent; the gains for the other two models test transfer of GPT-4o-written docs.

abstract.text: DRAFT argues that human-written tool documentation is often incomplete, redundant or wrong for LLMs, and that an LLM can fix it by using the tool. For each API it runs a loop in which an explorer invents a query and calls the tool, an analyzer points out where the doc disagrees with what happened, and a rewriter produces a new doc. A similarity check keeps the explored queries diverse, and a stopping rule ends the loop when the doc stops changing. On ToolBench and RestBench the revised docs raise tool-use accuracy for GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini and Llama-3-70B.
